def move(terrain, start, duration_s, n_runs, seed):
    import numpy as np
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    N = 60
    dt = duration_s / (N - 1)
    times = np.linspace(0, duration_s, N)

    lat = np.full(n_runs, start[0], dtype=float)
    lon = np.full(n_runs, start[1], dtype=float)
    pts = np.empty((n_runs, N, 3), dtype=float)
    pts[:, 0, 0] = lat
    pts[:, 0, 1] = lon
    pts[:, 0, 2] = 0

    # Bearings SE approx 135 degrees = 3*pi/4, add small noise +/- 7.5 degrees
    base_bearing = 3 * np.pi / 4
    bearing_noise = (rng.uniform(-1, 1, n_runs) * (np.pi / 24))  # +/-7.5 degrees
    bearings = np.full(n_runs, base_bearing) + bearing_noise

    inside = terrain.inside(lat, lon)

    for i in range(1, N):
        # Compute slope at current points
        slope_deg = terrain.slope_deg(lat, lon)  # degrees
        # Move approx along contour: try to keep slope near zero by adjusting dist
        # but here choose dist fixed to terrain.cell_m

        # Move slightly but try to keep elevation constant
        # So sample small steps at bearing, then select step size by tobler speed

        # Compute elevation difference if stepping terrain.cell_m at bearing
        latn, lonn = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearings, terrain.cell_m)
        elev_now = terrain.elev(lat, lon)
        elev_next = terrain.elev(latn, lonn)
        d_elev = elev_next - elev_now
        speed = terrain.tobler_speed_ms(d_elev, terrain.cell_m)
        # Distance traveled in dt seconds but capped by terrain.cell_m
        dist = np.minimum(terrain.cell_m, speed * dt)
        # Offset actual step
        latn, lonn = terrain.offset(lat, lon, bearings, dist)

        # Clamp in box to avoid nonsense out of bounds
        latn, lonn = terrain.clamp(latn, lonn)

        lat[:] = latn
        lon[:] = lonn
        pts[:, i, 0] = lat
        pts[:, i, 1] = lon
        pts[:, i, 2] = times[i]

        # Update inside mask
        inside &= terrain.inside(lat, lon)

    return pts, inside
